items.excerpt: Sometimes struggling startups can be rescued and become profitable, while at other times it makes more sense to sell them. Flint Capital’s Dmitry Smirnov shares three tips to help VCs navigate the decision process.

items.title: 4 Questions Startup Founders Should Ask In Meetings With VCs

items.excerpt: What’s the best bet when the pressure shifts in your business from growth to profitability? Guest author Bryan House, president at Elastic Path, advises investing in your existing customer base via expansions and renewals and cutting costs in other areas.

items.excerpt: Today, the focus for most SaaS companies is on profitable revenue rather than growth, writes Bryan House, president at Elastic Path. In Part 2 of his Post-ZIRP survival series, House provides some tips to help founders keep their churn rates low.
items.title: A Post-ZIRP Survival Guide For Startups Part 2: Aligning Product And Customer Success

items.title: Storytelling Is The ‘Make Or Break’ Skill Founders Are Lacking

items.title: Addressing Security Gaps During M&A Is Critical

items.excerpt: The tariffs are only the latest incident showing how fragile our supply chain ecosystem can be, writes Laura Dow of CPG Sourcing. In this guest commentary she provides some big-picture steps businesses can follow to build a more resilient supply chain.
items.title: How To Develop Stopgap Sourcing Tactics In A Volatile Trade Environment

items.title: Startups Are Still Riding The Boozeless Booze Wave

items.excerpt: The velocity of innovation, particularly around AI, is collapsing the shelf life of software differentiation, write guest authors Rob Biederman and John Nylen, who share go-to-market tactics relevant in today’s quickly changing SaaS sales climate.

items.excerpt: AI is redefining software’s role, enabling products that perform end-to-end work, write guest authors Medha Agarwal and Noah Lin of Defy, who share four playbook stages that leading AI-first companies are using to scale.
items.title: New Value Models, New Playbooks: Tactics AI-First Companies Use To Scale

items.excerpt: The pace of giant funding rounds slowed a bit this week. However, we still did see some jumbo-sized deals in the mix, topped by a $355 million growth round for First Due, a software provider for emergency responders. Healthcare and AI were also significant sectors for funding.
items.title: The Week’s 10 Biggest Funding Rounds: Public Safety Leads, While Healthcare And Fintech Also See Big Deals

items.excerpt: Austin’s startup scene is stronger than ever. That’s the consensus among investors in the city, and it’s borne out by Crunchbase data, which shows startups headquartered in the Lone Star State’s capital raised a record $7.19 billion in venture funding in 2025.
